D018-D016_h001.question:
I’ve been off since last winter—maybe five or six months now. I keep seeing flashes of that night, like someone suddenly stepping out in front of me on the street, or the way headlights hit the pavement in the rain. It just comes out of nowhere, and my chest locks up. I can’t explain why it sticks so hard; it wasn’t even the worst thing that’s ever happened, but it won’t let go.

I used to love going out with friends, picking outfits, dancing at shows—now nothing feels fun. I’ll be in the middle of a shoot, and someone laughs, and I just feel… empty. Like I’m watching it through glass. And honestly, I’ve been blaming my ex for a lot of it—he was supposed to pick me up that night, but he didn’t. I know it’s not that simple, but I keep replaying it like he could’ve stopped it.

I’ve been forgetting things too—where I left my phone, client names, even appointments. Not like I’m distracted; it’s like my mind just blanks. And if someone walks into a room too fast, I flinch. Hard. Like my body’s always ready to run.

There’s this thought that loops sometimes: *What if it had been worse?* Over and over. I don’t do anything to stop it—it just won’t stop.
D018-D016_h001.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D016_h001.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D018-D016_h002.question:
I’ve been having this constant loop in my head—thoughts just show up out of nowhere, like whispers I can’t shut off. They’re not always about one thing; sometimes they twist into something else, and I can’t tell if they’re memories or just… junk. It’s been going on for a few months now, maybe longer. There are triggers, too—like loud voices or someone touching my shoulder when I don’t see them coming. I flinch hard, like my body’s electrified. And my mind? It goes blank for seconds, like fog rolls in and I forget what I was just doing.

I used to care about auditions, chasing roles, building a name. Now it all feels pointless. Even when I book something small, it doesn’t register. Feels like I’m watching someone else live my life. I know there’s something I’m supposed to feel ashamed about—something that happened, but I don’t like to talk about it. I also get angry at people who were there, who didn’t step in. Maybe it wasn’t their fault, but it’s easier to point the finger than sit with the guilt of feeling broken.

The thoughts keep coming, but I don’t do anything to stop them—no rituals, nothing. I just… wait for them to pass.
D018-D016_h002.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D016_h002.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D018-D016_h003.question:

It’s been going on for months. I don’t talk about it much, but I keep thinking… I should’ve caught the defect earlier. I was right there. If I’d just checked that batch myself, maybe none of it would’ve happened.

Lately, I can’t focus. Walking the line, inspecting parts—my head feels foggy, like I’m moving through water. My wife says I’m distant. I want to help around the house, fix the porch rail like I promised, but I just sit. No drive. 

And people… if someone walks in fast or comes up behind me, I jump. Once I knocked over a rack of tools. Embarrassing. 

There’s also this… hum in my head. Not a sound, more like a thought stuck on repeat—*what if, what if, what if.* I don’t know where it comes from. Doesn’t always connect to the accident.     D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D016_h003.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D018-D016_h004.question:

D018-D016_h006.question:

I remember pieces of that day—the static on the radio, the dispatcher from South County crying—but whole chunks are just… gone. And honestly, even when my niece makes me laugh or I get a compliment, it’s like the joy hits a wall. I don’t feel warm. I just feel tired.  

I yelled at a tech guy last week over a headset issue—just snapped, called him incompetent. I didn’t mean it. But sometimes the anger just *erupts*.  

And then there are the thoughts. They just loop—about harm, about mistakes. I can’t say where they come from. I don’t act on them. I just can’t stop hearing them.

    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D016_h007.question:

D018-D016_h008.question:
